title: Denver’s new license plate reader deal is for 50 cameras — less than half as many as Flock has now
summary: Denver City Council began reviewing a proposed $150,000, one-year contract with Axon for 50 license plate-reading cameras to replace its expiring Flock Safety contract, which had 111 cameras. The new system would have a 21-day retention period, no national database, and an invite-only sharing arrangement, addressing concerns raised after ICE accessed Denver's Flock data nearly 1,400 times.

key_quotes.quote: The $150,000 contract with Axon would be for a year and would include the installation of 50 license plate-reading cameras in public intersections in the city.
ICE agents were able to access Denver's data nearly 1,400 times in 2024 and 2025 before the city asked to be removed from Flock's national database last April.
The city plans to set the data retention period for Axon's cameras to only 21 days, nine days shorter than it was for Flock.

Denver's system also will be cut off from all other law enforcement agencies, and its overseers will create an invite-only sharing system with nearby law enforcement agencies that agree to abide by certain rules.
